thought.text: Devise is wired up. The custom model overrides auth lookup, so let me verify the stored password hash directly with BCrypt:

reasoning_content: Devise's mapping and `database_authenticatable` module are present. The reason `User.authenticate` doesn't exist is because the custom model's `find_for_database_authentication` is customized. Let me just verify the password hash directly using BCrypt against the stored encrypted password. This is the most robust verification method.

action.command: cd /workspace && export PATH=/usr/local/ruby/bin:$PATH PGPASSWORD=root && timeout 200 bin/rails runner 'u = User.find_by(email: "admin@consul.dev"); puts "bcrypt match: " + BCrypt::Password.new(u.encrypted_password).is_password?("Aa12345678").to_s; puts "confirmed_at set: " + !u.confirmed_at.nil?.to_s; puts "admin record: " + (u.administrator ? "yes" : "no")' 2>&1 | tail -3
